I'll think through this as the farmer and give a complete plan.

---

*Settling in to think about this year's farming...*

I've been working this land since I was twenty. Five mu isn't much, but it's enough to feed me and my wife, with a little cotton money left over. The children are grown and in the city now, so it's just the two of us. My back isn't what it was, but I still do most things by hand.

I split my land the usual way: four mu for wheat and then maize after — that's my food and some grain to sell. The other one mu I keep in cotton. My neighbor dropped cotton last year, said it wasn't worth it, but I've grown cotton my whole life and the price has been decent. I'll keep that one mu, at least this year.

**Wheat (4 mu):** I planted in mid-October last fall, same as always. Used seed I bought at the town shop — nothing fancy, the same variety the co-op sold. Before planting I spread two bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) across the four mu. In spring at green-up, I'll put down urea — about a bag for the four mu — and irrigate once. If it's dry, I'll water again at jointing. Pumping from the well costs money, so I try to do just two waterings. I spray once for weeds, that's it. Last year I got maybe 380 kg per mu. A good year would be 420.

**Maize (4 mu):** As soon as the wheat combine comes through in June, I have to hurry — my nephew helps me plant with his machine, I give him some grain or a bit of cash. No tilling, just plant into the stubble. I put a bag of compound fertilizer down with the seed, and later when the maize is knee-high I topdress urea, maybe half a bag. If July is dry I'll water once. Usually I don't spray unless there's armyworms. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

**Cotton (1 mu):** I plant in late April after it warms up. I use a bit more fertilizer on cotton — it's hungry. One application of compound before planting, and urea when it starts flowering. Cotton needs more spraying — bollworm, aphids — I spray maybe three or four times through the summer. My wife helps with the picking starting in September, it takes us weeks. I get maybe 230 kg of lint per mu. Not as much as the young farmers with better seeds, but I know this variety.

I try to keep my spending low. Two bags of compound, three bags of urea, some pesticide for the cotton, a little diesel for the well. My cash reserve matters more than squeezing out more yield. That's how I've lasted 54 years on this land.
